category_title: Students with externalizing behavior problems including work refusal and temper tantrums
minimal_context: The student is participating in a lunchtime 4-square handball game with other students.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright, let's start the 4-square handball game. Remember to follow the agreed rules and respectfully take turns while you wait.

STUDENT: I'm in the square now. I'm going to stay in and beat everyone.

TUTOR: That ball bounced out of bounds. You are out, so please step out so the next person can play.

STUDENT: No way! I didn't get out! I'm not going to the back of the line to wait with the other nine kids!

TUTOR: You have to follow the rules like everyone else. Please step out of the square.

STUDENT: (Screams and throws the handball across the playground) It's not fair! I'm not moving and I'm not letting anyone else play!

options.A: Make regulative discourses explicitly visible to the student and unpack what they need to do during the game.
options.B: Reinforce the student with a sticker of their favorite rugby league team on a daily basis.
options.C: Change the 4-square playing routine by taking names out of a hat at random to nominate the competitors.
options.D: Implement organization techniques such as a two-pocket folder for daily work, a signed homework journal, and desk supply holders.
